trust_decision.summary: Whether a scrape URL on a lookalike host may be fetched at all is decided at the head of PixelDrainCrawler.fetch by exact membership of self.origin.host in SUPPORTED_DOMAINS, before file()/folder()/filesystem() issue any request carrying the Basic-auth API key; the routing that lets a lookalike host reach this crawler is the substring match in ScrapeMapper._best_match.

landing_point.why: The report says the API key goes to unverified sites; the reader lands on the crawler's URL router, which dispatches to file()/folder()/filesystem(), each of which calls PixelDrainAPI.text() with the key header built at pixeldrain.py:289-290.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI/input-file URL dispatch: ScrapeMapper._send_to_crawler -> Crawler.run -> PixelDrainCrawler.fetch for any host that substring-matches a registered domain (scrape_mapper.py:248-253)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route is available to dismiss: the u file, l folder, d filesystem (including the recursive subfolder() call at pixeldrain.py:218-222) and text-file link routes all issue their authenticated requests below fetch(), so the one gate covers every route and there is no plausible out-of-scope argument.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate scraping of the six other supported domains (pixeldrain.net, pixeldra.in, pixeldrain.nl/.biz/.tech/.dev) and the proxy route that is rewritten to pixeldrain.com: a fix that compares origin.host to PRIMARY_URL.host or DOMAIN instead of SUPPORTED_DOMAINS breaks them, including the live pixeldrain.net test case. Secondary: _make_scrape_mapper_keys deliberately strips 'www.' (crawler.py:998-1002), so a www subdomain is admitted by the router but rejected by an exact-membership list.

O6_input_shapes: subdomain of an unlisted parent host

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second consumer of the now-decoupled PixelDrainAPI (e.g. OnePaceCrawler resolving a /l/<id> list) that calls api.file/folder/filesystem directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: API.origin reads the global ORIGIN context var (crawler.py:994-995), not PRIMARY_URL, so the key follows whatever scrape item is in flight; onepace.py:46,100 already builds pixeldrain list URLs, so having it call the API instead of re-dispatching is a one-line change a maintainer would plausibly make.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The PixelDrainProxyCrawler (a mirror/wrapper class for pd.cybar.xyz and pd.1drv.eu.org) gaining the same API-key headers as the primary crawler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already rewrites proxy URLs onto pixeldrain.com, so a maintainer wanting premium limits through the proxy would attach the same auth header there while leaving its fetch() without a host gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A GoFile-style crawler refactored onto the decoupled API class so its request URL comes from API.origin (the in-flight scrape item's host) instead of module constants, while _prepare_headers still attaches the Bearer key
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: gofile already attaches a credential in _prepare_headers (gofile.py:109-110) and has no host gate in fetch (gofile.py:112-121); the pixelDrain #1939-#1943 commits did exactly this refactor - dedicated API class reading ORIGIN - while gofile still builds URLs from the constants at gofile.py:19-20, so porting it is a natural follow-up a maintainer would write.

O9_family: Exposure of a stored credential through improper host validation (CWE-200 information exposure / CWE-20 input validation) in crawl-URL dispatch

O10_build.toolchain: uv_build backend + uv.lock; pytest + pytest-asyncio, ruff
O10_build.project_tests: tests/crawlers/test_cases/pixeldrain.py driven by tests/crawlers/test_crawlers.py (Crawler.handle_media_item mocked, HTTP not mocked); the crawler_test_case marker is declared as making actual network requests (pyproject.toml:124), and selection is via pytest --test-crawlers pixeldrain. The fix adds one case to that file expecting 0 results.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Put the host check inside the ["u", file_id] branch (or inside file()), leaving the l folder and d filesystem branches - which also issue authenticated API calls - wide open.

out_of_scope_notes: The root cause is generic: ScrapeMapper._best_match (cyberdrop_dl/scrape_mapper.py:535) routes any host containing a registered domain string to that crawler. Other crawlers also lack a host gate in fetch (e.g. gofile.py:112-121) but build their request URLs from module constants (gofile.py:19-20), so no same-shape key leak was confirmed outside PixelDrain. Not pursued.

MediaItem.serialize (cyberdrop_dl/url_objects.py:208-214) includes the headers dict, so with dump_json enabled the same Basic-auth key is written to the local jsonl log; a different exposure of the same secret, not the advisory's third-party leak, not pursued.
